title: fix: prevent Gateway shutdown failures after in-place updates
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway shutdown failing with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` after an in-place update replaces the running installation's hashed bundles.

Related: #159699, whose published 2026.9.6 update proof exposed this failure.

## User Impact

Gateways containing this fix can finish cleanup after their package is replaced. This is fixed forward for updates **from** a release containing the fix: installing the candidate cannot repair code already running in an older Gateway, including 2026.9.6. Final transcript speech and deterministic notes are saved during shutdown; model notes can be regenerated afterward.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cleanup consumes state, callbacks, and module promises retained by the subsystem that created the resources. Transcript admission stays in its lightweight owner; Browser relay and Chrome MCP teardown use existing lazy module references; provider, MCP view, discarded-plugin-startup, and worker-artifact cleanup avoid first-loading implementations during retirement. Optional transcript inference is fenced during shutdown.

Worker preparation resolves one cached cleanup module in the pool's detached context before creating resources. Cancellation joins preparation and preserves caller-owned input settlement. Loading during worker preparation preserves the native hook relay's import budget. No Gateway-wide preload, startup budget increase, or timeout relaxation is added.

The audit covered session-end drain, plugin/channel close, sidecars, memory/database cleanup, and restart handoff. Loading a module elsewhere in the process is insufficient: Node can still resolve a new importer's first import against replaced files. Ordinary startup work and already-admitted turn execution remain separate from this cleanup contract.

## Evidence

### W9: tooling CI attribution and local stop report

The six requested job logs ran merge `2382ffd4742e63765e38b04ac3d2866a6c30b109` (PR head `f2e9db60beab8eb280ec4d911d8a320840514665` into main `3e05f6b380cd2d6f68b6205109aacdb5a201d836`). Both root causes came from that newer main, not this PR:

- Jobs `110167927941`, `110167927923`, `110167927868`, `110167927827`, and `110167927826` contain respectively 16, 5, 2, 8, and 1 unique failing cases. Main commit `588b5d7d50b7` added the `openclaw-state-maintenance-context.ts` import at `src/state/openclaw-state-db-async-lifecycle.ts:18` without its wrapper inventory entry. Extraction failed before provisioner startup, cascading into private-store injection and main-refresh assertions. Main owner fix `b3b34beebe08` adds the missing inventory entry. A local extracted-source probe reproduced the exact missing-module error using the CI main lifecycle module; adding only the omitted module let the same provisioner reach normal argument validation.
- Job `110167927924` contains one unique failure: 17 expected-error annotations versus 16 registered entries. Main commit `45a3d1723847` added the intentional missing-session-key fixture at `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run-admission.session-file.test.ts:169`; it is absent from this PR head. A local scanner probe reproduced that exact additional file/excerpt. Main owner fix `bd1138797711` now registers it. The moved MCP singleton assertion is unrelated; no inventory allowance was broadened here.

No W9 source/test/tooling changes: net **0 LOC**. The wrapper inventory already includes the PR's shared lazy-runtime dependency. No duplicate main fixes, commit, force-push, rebase, workflow rerun, or auto-merge re-arm was performed. The PR remains open and mergeable at the original head with its existing squash auto-merge request armed.

Validation on unchanged `f2e9db60`: the full six-file selection finished **344 passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped** across **5 passing files and 1 failing file** in **3156.76 s**. All runnable originally reported failing cases passed. The unsupported-filesystem case is skipped on macOS. The additional local failure is the macOS-only `materializes full cold/warm PR siblings, then preserves native sparse transitions` case at `test/scripts/pr-worktree-provision.test.ts:386`: it exceeded its unchanged 120-second limit at **143.497 s**. One isolated diagnostic replay failed at **134.309 s** (**1 failed, 16 filtered/skipped**, **141.75 s** Vitest duration). Its test and provisioning owner are unchanged by this PR, but the timeout's causal attribution remains unresolved; host load is context, not proof of cause. No timeout, assertion, or test was weakened. This is the W9 stop-report blocker.

Commands:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/pr-wrapper-source-closure.test.ts test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts test/scripts/pr-wrappers.test.ts test/scripts/type-suppression-inventory.test.ts test/scripts/pr-worktree-provision.test.ts test/scripts/pr-main-refresh.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/pr-worktree-provision.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'materializes full cold/warm PR siblings, then preserves native sparse transitions'
node scripts/check-changed.mjs --timed -- test/scripts/pr-wrapper-source-closure.test.ts test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts test/scripts/pr-wrappers.test.ts test/scripts/type-suppression-inventory.test.ts test/scripts/pr-worktree-provision.test.ts test/scripts/pr-main-refresh.test.ts
```

The scoped changed gate passed **17/17 checks**, including root tooling/scripts/E2E/other type graphs, scoped lint/format, and three Knip scans with zero entries. Separate type-aware oxlint passed for all **86 changed TypeScript files** using their core, extension, root-test, and script configs. Installed oxfmt passed for **88 matched changed files**; `git diff --check` passed. Full-candidate local Codex autoreview against merge base `503de53d455c6101e5194a7c960c2c110f434add` is **P2 scoped-clean**. No Gateway was started or stopped.


### W8: remaining CI failures

Fixed the two fixture failures reported by jobs 110152285448 and 110152281569. Startup shutdown now waits until the real stage-specific admission owner has parked behind suspension before closing; the assertion that drain finishes without reopening suspension is unchanged. The cases remain in their original suite position and share the same fixtures, but live in `server-startup-admission.test-support.ts` to satisfy the oversized-file growth ratchet. The SDK fixture now bundles the worker cleanup dependency used during preparation, while retaining its unexpected-import guard, child exit-status assertion, and awaited database cleanup. The clean-close receipt was merely part of the diagnostic message: the actual child failure was the rejected `temp-artifact-cleanup.ts` import. W8 changes no production code or public contracts; net +39 test/support LOC.

Attribution: both exact CI assertions reproduced locally on c91c65618bc9. A throwaway comparison using the relevant owner/test files from main 7e7c8d4ffe2a reproduced the startup failure unchanged (**84 passed, 1 failed**). That test supplies no `loadStartupPlugins`, so the PR's disposer capture is not executed. Its event-loop assumption predates this PR. The SDK failure is a PR-caused fixture mismatch with cleanup preloading; its main-file comparison instead reached the existing 5-second `native-same-store parent` timeout on the loaded host, so that comparison is not claimed as passing evidence.

Validation: **167 tests passed across nine files**, covering both failing files, Gateway startup/connection/admission siblings, transcript sidecar cleanup, and worker cleanup/retirement. After the fixture extraction, the full startup file passed again (**85/85**, **48.93 s** wrapper wall, **45.51 s** Vitest duration). The SDK file passed **1/1**, covering all three scenarios (**12.849 s** test execution; **204.94 s** wrapper wall including **111.255 s** worker-artifact preparation). Original failing CI case costs were **0.058 s** and **1.978 s** respectively; new-head CI timing is pending. No new test cases, process boots, sleeps, polling, or timeout relaxations were introduced. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --timed -- <three changed test/support paths>` passed all **21 checks** in **705.22 s**, including `gateway-server` and `messaging` tsgo graphs, scoped oxlint/oxfmt, line/assertion ratchets, and all three Knip scans (zero entries). Diff checks pass. Full-candidate local autoreview against merge base 503de53d455c is **P2 scoped-clean**. A summary-inference concern was reassessed with the actual tool dispatch and documented global-disable contract; no production change was warranted. No workflow was dispatched or rerun, and no Gateway was started or stopped.

- Built runtime smoke: started an isolated Gateway, waited for post-ready initialization and a successful `cron.status` read, renamed **7,011 hashed JS/MJS chunks**, then sent SIGTERM. It reported clean shutdown and exited **0** in **6,273 ms**, with no missing-module errors. Total smoke wall time: **106.77 s**. The fixture used private configuration/state, a free loopback port, and disabled plugins/channel/cron timers.
- Loader guards fail on the corresponding unpatched main code for transcript sidecar stop, Browser relay/Chrome MCP teardown, MCP view disposal, and worker-artifact retirement. Candidate cases pass. The request-context guard also failed before detached worker preparation and passes afterward.
- Focused consumers: **937 tests passed** across Gateway, transcripts, CLI, agents, plugins, and Browser. Final worker lifecycle siblings: **79 passed**. Startup import-boundary tests: **11 passed**.
- Builds: `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` passed in **437.53 s**, including 95 bundled plugins, published-updater compatibility bridges, SDK exports, and startup import guards. The final runtime refresh using the canonical `qaRuntime` profile passed in **109.96 s**.
- Types: `pnpm tsgo:core`, eight relevant core test graphs, root E2E/other graphs, and extension production/test graphs passed. Affected worker and CLI/MCP graphs were rechecked after follow-ups.
- Runtime value cycles and Madge: **zero**. Scoped type-aware lint, formatting, runtime-sidecar loader guards, line-count/assertion-safety ratchets, and diff checks passed. Resolve-undo is empty. Final full-candidate P2 review is clean. After resolving the documentation-only rebase conflict, core types, focused shutdown regressions, the runtime build, and the chunk-removal smoke passed again on the rebased head.

- Maintainer review follow-up (`refactor: drop lazy and aliased shutdown cleanup imports`, net −6 LOC): `closeCliResources` reads dispatcher-pool facts from its existing static `provider-runtime-lifecycle` import, so no teardown path in this build lazily imports that module. The stable `tsdown` entry stays: `scripts/lib/update-compat-chunks.mts` bridges published builds' hashed `provider-runtime-lifecycle-*.js` chunks to a current chunk that still exports those facts. Removing it broke every CI shard with `Cannot bridge ... no equivalent current export`; restoring it lets the `previous release update compat chunks` postbuild phase pass locally. The canonical `stopActiveManagedProviderLocalServices` name replaces a naming-only alias. MCP cleanup callers import `releaseSessionMcpRuntime` and `completeDeferredSessionMcpRuntimeRetirement` from their owner module instead of a forwarding re-export. Chrome MCP teardown's `peek()` is exact: every session-creating route call runs after `ensureTabAvailable`, which loads the adapter through `getChromeMcpModule()`. Re-run: 29 targeted consumer files (bundle-mcp, mcp-app, run-loop, runtime-cleanup, run-main.exit, MCP runtime/manager) gave 847 passed and 1 failed. That failure was `settles private MCP acquisition cancellation at ready` (`agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts:2298`, cleanup-failure check at `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.ts:1110`) during a 506 s loaded run. The full file replayed in its original order passed 114/114, which is recorded here as unexplained; it is not treated as fixed. `agent-command-local.test.ts` could not run locally because the Gateway-artifact preparation fence refused runtime preparation, so CI covers it. Import cycles are 0, lint and format are clean, core, extension and root production/test type graphs pass (`test-root-other` was interrupted at the 15-minute budget), and local-candidate Codex autoreview P2 is scoped-clean.

- Rebased onto `main` e92ab30a (toolchain moved to TypeScript 7.1-dev, Vitest 5): `main` split worker construction into `src/infra/worker-task-pool-worker.ts`, so temp-artifact cleanup is now imported statically there, and this PR's superseded asynchronous preparation path and its two interleaving tests were removed (−104 LOC against the earlier PR revision). CI follow-ups: the launchd fixture uses the canonical `stopActiveManagedProviderLocalServices`; the browser relay integration fixtures (`gateway-relay-ingress`, `gateway-relay-route`, `bootstrap.chromium`) load the handler through `getGatewayExtensionRelayModule()` like production does; Knip treats `provider-runtime-lifecycle` as an entry because published-update bridges consume `hasManagedProviderLocalServices`; the admission-identity fixture awaits its async database-close owners. Locally: launchd 4/4, browser relay and shutdown suites 24/24, all Knip `deadcode` scans 0 entries, oxfmt/oxlint clean, and Codex autoreview P2 is scoped-clean on the full rebased candidate. The runtime inventory and npm package-planning failures in the previous CI run were already fixed on `main` (5b76930a9b6f, 172043bbac46). `reply-turn-admission.module-identity` could not be judged locally: it hit its 5 s probe bound at 8.2 s with the host at load average 65–80, so this CI run is its proof. Package planning could not run locally because the Gateway-artifact fence detected running operator services.

- Worker cleanup preload follow-up (`f228f3f926b0`): replaces the rebase's static import with one cached dynamic loader awaited by task preparation in the detached pool context, before `prepareWorker` creates resources. Worker construction stays synchronous. The interim preload reproduced **4 failed / 3 passed** cleanup cases; the repair passes **124/124 worker-pool tests across 12 files** in **151.78 s**, including all four guards. Core production types and all **27** selected test graphs (including infra) passed. Scoped oxlint, oxfmt, diff checks, and full-candidate local Codex autoreview P2 are clean. The native relay CLI source closure has **149 modules, zero forbidden imports, and zero unresolved edges**. The existing-dist CLI bootstrap guard passes; fresh emitted-bundle proof remains for CI because no full build was run. The changed-lanes run stopped at the 15-minute host budget during the broader deprecated-API audit, after typechecks passed; scoped lint then passed separately. Net **+20 production LOC**; no tests added or changed.

- Squashed to one commit and rebased onto `main` 503de53d (the PR had gone `dirty`), resolving seven conflicts onto `main`'s newer shapes: the shared MCP acquisition helper, transcript fixtures, shared run-loop mocks and the worker `PostedTask` type. Worker artifact cleanup is now preloaded in detached task preparation instead of statically imported, which keeps `chalk`/`tslog` out of the native hook relay's static graph (the CI build guard failure on fae57845). Local results on the rebased candidate: 221 focused tests passed; core production types and six core-test graphs pass; Knip deadcode, the CLI bootstrap guard and a relay source traversal (0 forbidden imports) pass; oxfmt is clean; Codex autoreview P2 is scoped-clean. One local failure is recorded here rather than hidden: `transcripts-tool.account-ownership.test.ts` › "applies provider access to historical rows after the agent boundary" hit its 120 s timeout at 134 s with host load 104–140, then passed in an original-order standalone replay at 104 s. The replay does not prove a fix; this CI run is the judge. The remaining type graphs and oxlint were cut short by the local time budget and run in CI.

<details>
<summary>Measured test cost and fixture corrections</summary>

One-worker runs used `pnpm test <selected files> --maxWorkers=1`. The eight-file regression run took **213.99 s** wall. The final five-file worker selection took **59.11 s**, including shared compiler preparation. Measured file execution times:

| File/owner | Test time |
| --- | ---: |
| Gateway transcript sidecar | 0.099 s |
| Transcript live summaries (14 cases) | 42.041 s |
| Browser rejection cleanup (7 cases) | 0.126 s |
| Browser shutdown races (2 cases) | 0.018 s |
| MCP materialized-view cleanup | 0.016 s |
| Provider service settlement (4 cases) | 0.304 s |
| Worker artifact cleanup (9 cases) | 0.438 s |
| Worker retirement failures (12 cases) | 0.089 s |
| Gateway import boundaries (11 cases) | 33.092 s |

The summary tests exercise real SQLite-backed accepted-speech persistence and finalization, which a loader-only mock cannot prove. The import guard traverses real source graphs; batching and caching import facts reduced its kernel case from a 120 s timeout to 21.3 s without changing assertions or budgets. Existing CLI consumer files took 75.837 s and 5.779 s; their changes only adapt mocks.

The retirement fixture now waits for fake-worker task admission. A diagnostic also demonstrated that concurrent first imports could resolve one mocked and one real cleanup export; retaining one loader promise gives all workers the same owner-held export. The transcript sidecar fixture registers its mocks before importing the now-lightweight owner. Smoke setup follows the current published launcher inventory and readiness parser, and waits for post-ready initialization before removing files.

No new process boots, sleeps, polling, or worker pins were introduced into CI tests. CI timing is pending; no workflow was dispatched or rerun for proof.

</details>
